chunks: He said: Woe be to you,

I am not like you. Certainly, Allāh, the Sublime, has made it obligatory on true leaders that they should maintain themselves at the level of low people, so that the poor do not cry over their poverty!

key_terms.يَتَبَيَّغَ: To cry out / weep in distress

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imams live modestly according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) highlights the theological principle of *tadhalluf* (humility) and *tashabbuh* (conformity), where Imams are obligated to mirror the social and economic status of the common people to prevent alienation. This practice ensures that the disparity between leadership and the populace does not become a source of sorrow or resentment for the poor, reinforcing the Imam's role as a relatable guide rather than a distant ruler.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Then he replied: Woe be to you,

I am not like you. Certainly, Allāh, the Sublime, has made it obligatory on true leaders that they should maintain themselves at the level of low people so that the poor do not cry over their poverty. [1]
